user.title: Sun Shading
user.description:
Sun Shading simulates the shadows cast on your windows by the real buildings, terrain and trees around them, from the Strasbourg Eurométropole 3D open data.

Building a zone downloads a few gigabytes of 3D tiles and takes tens of minutes — the next screen tells you how many tiles, how much disk and how long on this machine. The entry is created right away: the sidebar panel and a progress sensor appear immediately, and the map opens when the build finishes.

menu_options.external: Use data built outside Home Assistant

build.title: Zone to simulate
build.description: The map is centred on this point, prefilled with your Home Assistant location. Only the Strasbourg Eurométropole is covered by the source data.

data_description.location: The radius drives everything else: 500 m ≈ 9 tiles and ~1 GB downloaded, 1000 m ≈ 29 tiles and ~3 GB, 1500 m ≈ 60 tiles and ~6 GB. Buildings, terrain and textures extend a little further so that off-map shadows still fall on the map.
data_description.title: Shown in the sidebar and used to name the entities and the data folder.

advanced.name: Advanced
advanced.description: Leave empty to derive everything from the radius above.

data_description.photomesh: The heaviest option by far: about 1 GB downloaded and 20-30 minutes for 200 m, plus ~370 MB of graphics memory when the viewer switches to it. Off by default.
data_description.photomesh_radius: 200 m is the tested value; cost grows with the square of the radius.
data_description.ortho_px: 8192 px ≈ 44 cm/px and 169 MB of graphics memory once decoded; 4096 px costs four times less and looks blurry when zoomed in.
data_description.shadow_lift: The 2022 aerial imagery has the shadows of that day baked into it, which add up to the simulated ones. 0.78 lifts them; 1 leaves them untouched.
data_description.obj_path: Path relative to the configuration folder. Replaces the simplified roof of one building with a hand-modelled one (see the repository documentation).
data_description.r_bati: Leave 0 to derive: displayed radius + 50 m, so that shadows cast from just outside the map still land on it.
data_description.r_terrain: Leave 0 to derive: displayed radius + 80 m, so the edge of the world is never visible.
data_description.r_arbres: Leave 0 to derive: same as the displayed radius.
data_description.r_textures: Leave 0 to derive: displayed radius + 50 m. Only affects the satellite view.
data_description.r_mnt_natif: Terrain kept at full resolution up to here, aggregated on a 10 m grid beyond. Leave 0 for 500 m.

error.out_of_coverage: No 3D tile covers this point: the source data only spans the Strasbourg Eurométropole.
error.radius_out_of_range: The radius must be between 100 m and 1500 m (beyond that the quantised local frame overflows).
error.obj_not_found: OBJ file not found, relative to the configuration folder.
error.no_manifest: No manifest.json in this folder: it is not a folder built by the pipeline.

abort.reconfigure_successful: Zone updated; it is rebuilt if needed.

init.title: Sun Shading
init.description: These settings apply immediately: nothing is rebuilt.

data_description.require_admin: The panel writes horizon masks and reads your covers; leave it on unless you want it to be viewable by everyone.
data_description.shadow_quality: 2048 costs about 30 MB of graphics memory, 4096 about 117 MB, 8192 about 470 MB — the single largest item in the scene. Capped at 4096 in Photo 3D mode. Viewers can still change it in the map.

advanced.name: Advanced
advanced.description: How masks are computed and read.

data_description.foliation: Four days of the year (1 January = 0): start and end of budburst, start and end of leaf fall. Deciduous trees let much more sun through when bare, and the two masks are blended along these ramps.
data_description.threshold: How much of the 50 cm probe square must be lit for “direct sun” to be declared.
data_description.azimuth_step: Degrees between two bands of a mask. A finer step costs proportionally more time when the page computes a mask (about 2 s at 1°).

set_opening.name: Set opening
set_opening.description: Creates or updates the “direct sun” sensor of an opening, from the horizon mask computed by the map. Called by the page; not meant to be typed by hand.

id.name: Identifier
id.description: Stable identifier of the opening (lowercase, no spaces).

name.name: Name
name.description: Readable name, which becomes the sensor's.

entry_id.name: Zone
entry_id.description: Config entry of the zone; required when several are configured.

point.name: Point
point.description: Probed point, in the map's local frame (x, y, z).

normal.name: Normal
normal.description: Normal of the surface at the probed point.

leafy.name: Leafy mask
leafy.description: [min, max] elevation bands per azimuth, deciduous trees in leaf.

bare.name: Bare mask
bare.description: [min, max] elevation bands per azimuth, deciduous trees bare.

threshold.name: Threshold
threshold.description: Lit fraction of the opening above which direct sun is declared.

foliation.name: Foliation dates
foliation.description: Four days (zero-based): start and end of budburst, start and end of leaf fall.

remove_opening.name: Remove opening
remove_opening.description: Removes an opening and its sensor.

id.name: Identifier
id.description: Identifier of the opening to remove.

entry_id.name: Zone
entry_id.description: Config entry of the zone; required when several are configured.

rebuild.name: Rebuild
rebuild.description: Rebuilds the zone from the source data. Already downloaded tiles are reused.
